prompt.en: Complete the sentence with a two-syllable word.

what_to_do.en: Tap the one word that fits.

stages.choice_rule: Four unique lowercase whole words from the roots word list. Exactly one choice is a two-syllable word that fills the hyphen and makes a sensible sentence. Vary the answer index. Tier 1 wrong choices are three one-syllable words that do not fit. Tier 2 uses one one-syllable meaning trap, one three-syllable word, and one one-syllable word that does not fit, with no second two-syllable choice. Tier 3 uses one one-syllable word that fits the meaning and one two-syllable word that does not fit. Correct spellings only.

gold_items.stem: Mom put a soft - on the bed.
We saw a - hop in the grass.
Dad gave me a - for school.
My kitten can drink - from a bowl.
A tiny - sat in the yard.
<NAME> wore a warm - in the cold snow.
Please pass the - and the jam at breakfast.

roots: Write one Grade 2 sentence about school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather, with exactly one hyphen where the word is missing.
Every stem word must come from the roots word list, aside from the hyphen blank and an optional <NAME> token.
Offer four whole-word choices from the roots list. Exactly one choice has two syllables and completes the sentence.
The answer must be a correctly spelled easy two-syllable word. Never make a one-syllable or three-syllable word the answer.
On tier 1, the three wrong choices are one-syllable words that do not fit the sentence.
On tier 2, include one one-syllable word that could fit the meaning, one three-syllable word, and one one-syllable word that does not fit.
On tier 3, include one one-syllable word that fits the meaning and one two-syllable word that does not fit the meaning.
Use correct spellings only. Do not use misspellings, brand names, real person names, or isolated sounds.
Vary answer_index across items. Do not describe a picture and do not invent audio files.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of about four to eight words. The correct choice is a common two-syllable word that completes the sentence. The other three choices are one-syllable words that do not fit. Use explain_key fits_two.
tier_rules.2: Grade-level stems. One choice is the two-syllable word that fits. One distractor is a one-syllable word that could fit the meaning. One distractor has three syllables. One distractor is a one-syllable word that does not fit. Use explain_key fits_two.
tier_rules.3: Near misses on longer kid sentences of up to ten words. One distractor is a one-syllable word that fits the meaning. One distractor is a two-syllable word that does not fit. Only one choice does both jobs. Use explain_key near_two.

fits_two.en: This word has two syllables and it completes the sentence.
fits_two.ko: 이 단어는 두 음절이고 문장을 완성합니다.

near_two.en: Only this word has two syllables and fits the sentence.
near_two.ko: 이 단어만 두 음절이면서 문장에 맞습니다.
